issue_context.title: failing yarn install does not stop further steps
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->
- have a wrong package url in package.json or no network connection
- run `rails assets:precompile`
### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->
rake task fails completely
### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->
task proceeds to precompiling resulting in possible runtime errors
### System configuration
**Rails version**:
5.2
**Ruby version**:
2.6.2

the issue is with 
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/43288a053feecf7cdbe74e61f3ca2038d976e9f4/railties/lib/rails/tasks/yarn.rake#L11
we should probably add `or exit!` to this line. I can craft a PR if you're ok with this
comments:
I think `raise` is more appropriate than `exit!`. This allows to switch to the using `exception: true` option when only support Ruby >= 2.6.  Anyway, I agree that it should be an error. Can you create a PR?
This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not been commented on for at least three months.
The resources of the Rails team are limited, and so we are asking for your help.
If you can still reproduce this error on the `5-2-stable` branch or on `master`, please reply with all of the information you have about it in order to keep the issue open.
Thank you for all your contributions.

review_comments:
I want to avoid run `yarn install` inside the test.

The fact that the tests passed in the original condition mean that the JS library is unnecessary for testing.
So I think better to generate `package.json` that library specification is empty in the setup of `assets_test.rb`

i’m not sure it’s unnecessary, all the needed packages were already there - it’s just the package.json was wrong, so yarn install failed but something might be requiring modules and succeeding

I’ll use an empty package.json and see if anything fails
